candidates.selection_mechanism: CFG1/CFG2/CFG3 3-pin digital strap, confirmed via datasheet table: 1XX=5V, 000=9V, 001=12V, 011=15V, 010=20V. Alternates: single resistor on CFG1 (CFG2/3 float), or I2C (addr 0x22/0x23) when CFG2/3 free.
candidates.notes: LEAD. VBUS pin is sense-only (shorted to VHV), confirming the 5A path never runs through the chip - matches 'pass-through trigger board' framing. PG pin (10, open-drain active-low) drives the mandatory power-present LED directly but does not natively distinguish selected-profile-achieved vs 5V-fallback; that needs added compare circuitry at architecture stage. Best stock and price of all real candidates found.

candidates.selection_mechanism: ADDR/ORIENT pin floating = GPIO mode. SNK_VSET + SNK_ISET are analog resistor-divider inputs that jointly set requested voltage/current (not a clean 3-bit digital table - needs switched resistor taps per DIP position). I2C mode also available (ADDR tied to VDD/GND) but unused here (no MCU).
candidates.max_v: 28V/3.25A in GPIO mode (48V/5A only in I2C mode, unused)
candidates.notes: ALTERNATE. FAULT/OUT2 pin (13) pulls HIGH specifically when 'the power adapter cannot supply the required voltage or current' - closer native fit than CH224K's plain PG for the requirements' visible-fallback ask. Traded off against QFN package (leadless, flagged per requirement) and a less DIP-switch-natural analog selection interface.

candidates.selection_mechanism: Same CFG1/CFG2/CFG3 family mechanism as CH224K, extended for AVS/PPS/EPR up to 28V.
candidates.notes: PASSED OVER: real WCH-brand listing is at 0 stock; DFN-EP is leadless; more capability (EPR/140W) than the brief needs. Two other 'CH224Q' search hits (C9900166627, C9900265230) are JLCPCB-Assembly generic placeholder SMT-footprint entries ($0.0393, no datasheet, category 'SMT') - not real orderable parts, excluded as search noise.

candidates.selection_mechanism: CFG1/CFG2/CFG3 family mechanism plus integrated NMOS gate-driver (DRV) and current-sense (ISP/ISN) pins for a power-switch role.
candidates.notes: PASSED OVER: QFN-20 (leadless, more pins than CH224K's ESSOP-10) with integrated power-switch/current-sense features this design doesn't need (VBUS is bare copper pass-through per requirements, not gated by the controller). No upside over CH224K here. Datasheet URL not returned by search; covered by the same combined CH224-family manual pulled for CH224K.

candidates.selection_mechanism: SEL pin is a 3-level selector (High/Float/GND) giving only 3 max-voltage ceilings: High=20V, Float=15V, GND=5V. A separate part number, IP2721_MAX12, gives 12V/9V/5V instead. No single populated part covers 5/9/12/15/20V.
candidates.max_v: 20V, but only 3 of the 5 required levels on any one part
candidates.notes: DISQUALIFIED: hard functional gap, not a preference call - cannot cover the required 5-profile set with one part. Also requires an external NMOS in the VBUS power path (VBUSG pin drives its gate) - extra BOM the CH224K/HUSB238 topology avoids. Currently 0 stock too. Package itself (TSSOP-16) is non-leadless and would otherwise be attractive.

candidates.selection_mechanism: None found for live/runtime use. Cypress's own description: 'highly-integrated pre-programmed USB Type-C port controller targeting electronic devices that have legacy [barrel-connector] power inputs' - fixed single-voltage output configured once via the EZ-PD Configuration Utility over I2C/OTP. Datasheet grepped for VSEL/pin-strap/preset/hardware-select - no hits.
candidates.notes: DISQUALIFIED for this design: no hardware pin-strap for live multi-profile selection; would need an external I2C host/MCU to reprogram between profiles, which this MCU-less trigger board does not have. Same underlying reason FUSB302 is out.

candidates.selection_mechanism: n/a - not a self-contained PD sink. FUSB302 is a Type-C CC/PHY transceiver only; all PD sink policy (PDO parsing, profile request, GoodCRC, negotiation state machine) runs in external MCU firmware.
candidates.notes: DISQUALIFIED: needs a host MCU to run the PD stack (why every FUSB302 breakout pairs it with a microcontroller). This board has no MCU by design (selector is DIP switch/jumper/button per the brief). Hard disqualifier, not a package/stock issue - included only because the task named it explicitly.
